# Android platform TLS support

Source-derived JNI classes based on rustls-platform-verifier-android 0.2.0. The original AAR and CertificateVerifier.kt remain pristine; UPSTREAM.json records their fixed revisions and hashes. Three ordered patches select Android's default host trust configuration (rather than a standalone explicit AndroidCAStore) remove upstream test-only branches from the release helper, and give each executor worker its own non-thread-safe CertificateFactory while protecting root-cache lookups with a short monitor. Certificate checking and revocation policy remain upstream's implementation.

The AAR changes application-wide networkSecurityConfig. Only the derived classes.jar is packaged, with both upstream licenses and provenance as Java resources. Kotlin stdlib is an explicit runtime dependency in the Maven POM. R8 retains the three JNI-facing classes and may shrink the Kotlin runtime. No Kotlin Gradle compiler plugin or AndroidX dependency is added. Real Android CA, pinning and revocation behavior still requires device tests.

Rebuild on Linux using `python3 scripts/rebuild-android-tls-verifier.py` (check) or `--write` (two independent builds must agree). `--fetch-tools` downloads missing build-only compiler jars from Maven Central and verifies their recorded hashes. `--jdk`, `--android-jar` and `--gradle-cache` override local input locations; see `--help`. The builder needs JDK17, API36 stubs and bubblewrap. Networkless subprocesses see read-only inputs, an empty environment and a bounded private scratch filesystem. Only three bounded Java8 class files are retained, in a deterministic jar. Kotlin/compiler/stub inputs are hashed; ordinary SDK builds consume the checked-in jar without compiling Kotlin.

`scripts/testing/android_tls_selector_probe.py` exercises the actual jar with a dummy JCA provider under the same isolation. It verifies factory selection only, never certificate or device policy behavior. `scripts/test-android-tls-source-contract.sh` combines rebuild equality, pristine upstream selector and derived selector checks.
